intended_object: An m-strongly convex function on a convex set s of a real normed space: s is convex and f(tx+(1−t)y) ≤ t f(x) + (1−t) f(y) − (m/2) t(1−t)‖x−y‖² for all x, y ∈ s and t ∈ [0,1]. This comes from the docstring and the name.
explanation:
The definition unfolds to `UniformConvexOn s (fun r ↦ m/2 * r^2) f`. That says s is convex and, for all x, y ∈ s and all a, b ≥ 0 with a + b = 1, f(a x + b y) ≤ a f(x) + b f(y) − a·b·(m/2)‖x − y‖². This is exactly the standard definition of m-strong convexity on a normed space.

The definition also accepts any real m. For m = 0 the condition reduces to ordinary convexity. For m < 0 it is a weaker condition, which is a harmless generalisation; the usual notion is the case m > 0.

The setting is the natural one. The domain is any real normed space, and real-valued functions are standard here. The squared-norm modulus needs a norm, so the definition cannot be stated in less structure. Mathlib has no other, more general definition of strong convexity.
